title: Vietnam’s R&I credit rating rises to BBB- with stable outlook
summary:
Vietnam has entered investment grade for the first time after R&I raised its foreign-currency issuer rating to BBB- from BB+.
The outlook moved to stable from positive, with R&I citing growth fundamentals, reforms, fiscal space and shock resilience.
The finance ministry said the upgrade should support investor confidence and long-term capital mobilisation.

title: Bangladesh’s PMI falls to 48.6 in September as manufacturing contracts
summary:
Bangladesh’s PMI fell to 48.6 in September from 49.9 in August, as manufacturing and construction contracted and services remained weak. 
Agriculture continued to expand for the 13th consecutive month. 
Businesses cited rising costs, fuel price hikes, energy shortages, weak consumer demand and limited credit access as major challenges.

title: Egypt, South Korea launch CEPA talks, elevate strategic ties
summary:
Egypt and South Korea launched negotiations on a CEPA and upgraded ties to a strategic partnership.
Following summit talks in Seoul, the leaders signed or revised 12 co-operation documents covering defense, shipbuilding, clean energy and technology. 
They pledged to expand trade, investment and industrial co-operation, while bilateral trade reached $874 million in January-August 2026.

title: India targets $1 trn exports in current year: Goyal
summary:
India has set a $1 trillion export target for the current year after recording $863 billion in exports last year, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said in a summit.
He said the goal implies nearly 16 per cent growth, against expected global trade growth of about 2.5-3 per cent. 
Goyal urged CII to create FTA utilisation desks in every state council for MSMEs.

title: South Indian cotton yarn sees mixed trend as raw cotton costs rise
summary:
India’s cotton yarn markets were mixed, with Mumbai seeing ₹3–6 (~$0.03–0.06) per kg gains in several counts but ₹2–5 declines in selected varieties as weak fabric demand and payment constraints weighed on sentiment.
Tiruppur yarn rose ₹2–3 per kg as costlier cotton prompted stock replenishment.
Gujarat cotton jumped ₹1,500–2,000 per candy on firmer ICE futures and slower arrivals.

title: Vietnam & US close to finalising reciprocal trade agreement
summary:
Vietnam and the US have settled most of a reciprocal, fair and balanced trade agreement, with only technical issues left, the industry ministry said.
Seven official rounds have been held since April 2025, alongside ministerial and technical-level talks.
The US was Vietnam's top export market at $140 billion in the first nine months; the surplus rose 23.8 per cent to $122.62 billion.

title: US Upland cotton export sales fall 19%; shipments rise 8%: USDA
summary:
US cotton export sales fell in the week ended October 1, 2026, with 2026–27 Upland net sales down 19 per cent week on week to 165,100 RB, though 14 per cent above the four-week average.
Vietnam led Upland buying at 61,800 RB, followed by Pakistan and India; Upland shipments rose 8 per cent to 161,600 RB.
Pima sales recovered to 3,300 RB, but shipments dropped 69 per cent to 2,900 RB.

title: CMAI welcomes GST reforms, flags higher tax on garments
summary:
CMAI welcomed GST procedural reforms limiting officers’ prosecution powers and removing arrest powers but criticised the 18 per cent GST on garments priced above ₹2,500 (~$26).
It had sought an increase in the price threshold to at least ₹10,000 (~$103), saying this would have significantly boosted garment consumption and sales during the forthcoming festive season.

title: Drewry WCI dips 1.87% as China’s Golden Week hits demand
summary:
Drewry’s World Container Index fell 1.87 per cent to $4,351 per FEU in the week ending October 8 as China’s Golden Week slowed East–West cargo flows.
Transpacific rates from Shanghai to Los Angeles and New York fell 3 per cent and 2 per cent, while Asia–Europe saw Rotterdam down 2 per cent.
Rates may stay stable next week, though Suez capacity and geopolitics may keep the market volatile.

title: ICE cotton futures edge lower ahead of USDA WASDE report
summary:
US ICE cotton futures settled marginally lower on Thursday as traders awaited the USDA WASDE report, with the December 2026 contract down 9 points at 79.94 cents per pound.
The contract stayed 106 points higher for the week, while volume eased to 40,731 lots and open interest remained near a record high.
US export sales totalled 224,404 bales, led by Vietnam, Pakistan, China and India.

title: Myanmar garment closures: Is responsible exit now a buyer risk?
summary:
Myanmar’s garment closures are turning human-rights due diligence into a commercial and reputational risk for buyers still sourcing from the country.
Teng Hui in Yangon is preparing a temporary suspension after reduced orders, with 2,355 of 2,610 workers seeking transfers.
Japan’s Myanmar imports rose to $1.68 billion in 2025, with clothing and accessories at 78.5 per cent.

title: US' AAFA targets online counterfeits in USTR review submission
summary:
AAFA has asked the US Trade Representative to include Facebook, Instagram, Alibaba.com, AliExpress and DHGate in its 2026 Notorious Markets report on counterfeiting and piracy. 
The US apparel and footwear association said its products remain among US Customs' top 10 seized commodities in FY25. 
It said 41 per cent of 39 counterfeit goods tested in 2026 failed safety standards.

title: Canada's Lululemon appoints Gauger as president, Godsey as COO
summary:
Lululemon has created a new Senior Leadership Team structure, appointing Maggie Gauger as president & chief product officer and Joseph Godsey as chief operating officer, effective October 26, 2026.
The company is also seeking brand, communications, technology and strategy chiefs, while Nikki Neuburger and Ted Dagnese will depart on November 6.

title: Cambodia, Indonesia ship $5.6 bn in US apparel: China losing ground?
summary:
Cambodia and Indonesia supplied $5.60 billion of US apparel imports in January-July 2026, overtaking China’s $5.28 billion as the US market contracted.
TexPro data shows imports fell 8.30 per cent to $44.06 billion, with China and India driving most of the net decline.
Gains came mainly from stronger category positions, but value pressure and textile dependencies remain risks.

title: India’s garment exports fell $575 mn. What went wrong?
summary:
India’s garment exports fell 10.38 per cent to $4.967 billion in April–July 2026, a $575.49-million loss, while yarn-and-thread exports rose 17.15 per cent to $1.846 billion.
The US drove 69 per cent of the net fall, with exports there down 21.41 per cent to $1.466 billion.
Recovery needs stronger volumes, market share, factory utilisation and jobs, not just a less severe contraction.

title: Australia’s apparel imports decline to $1.47 bn in July-Aug 2026
summary:
Australia’s apparel imports fell 3.37 per cent to Au$2.118 billion (~$1.48 billion) in July-August 2026, while imports of textile yarn, fabrics and made-up articles declined 3.40 per cent to Au$767 million.
Fibre imports rose slightly to Au$23 million, but textile fibre exports eased 14.44 per cent to Au$1.155 billion and cotton exports fell 17.70 per cent in August.
ABS data showed mixed trade.

title: Bangladesh's apparel exports to US rebound in August
summary:
Bangladesh's apparel exports to the US rose to $734.6 million in August 2026 from $660.9 million a year earlier, OTEXA data showed.
China and Vietnam posted modest gains, while Cambodia and India declined in August shipments to the US.
For January-August, Bangladesh shipments were about $5.39 billion, down 4.17 per cent from about $5.62 billion.

title: Bangladesh-Russia apparel trade falls 61.5%: Who takes the orders?
summary:
Bangladesh’s direct RMG exports to Russia fell 61.5 per cent from FY2020-21 to FY2025-26, with July-August FY2026-27 shipments down 33.95 per cent year on year.
TexPro shows China, Türkiye, Italy and India recovered after 2022, shipping $4.71 billion in 2025, 9.2 per cent above 2021.
Payment bans and unsettled routes remain the main constraint for exporters.

title: Rodinia’s €4 mn Portugal move: Is nearshore apparel ready to scale?
summary:
Rodinia Generation has raised €4 million (~$4.5 million) to scale O-factory technology at a Portugal facility planned for early 2027.
It says automation, on-demand manufacturing and shorter supply chains can cut landed costs for short-run fashion.
EU-27 textile and clothing imports are €122 billion, twice exports of €61 billion; around one-third of products sold in Europe are made in China.

title: France's Christian Dior appoints two independent board directors
summary:
Christian Dior has co-opted Tony Estanguet and Xavier Musca as independent directors, effective immediately, replacing Nicolas Bazire and Maria Luisa Loro Piana.
The appointments follow the Arnault family group's proposed corporate-structure simplification, which would trigger a mandatory tender offer for Christian Dior shares without a squeeze-out.
